_comment: Per-model Odoo version and edition facts for Layer 1 (DECISIONS.md 17, 17a).
Verified against real Odoo source -- community 14.0-19.0 from odoo/odoo, and ENTERPRISE
17.0/18.0/19.0 from official +e source packages. Not from memory: DECISIONS.md 12's
recalled list was corrected on one entry and was missing another entirely.
A model absent from `models` below is present, unchanged, in every supported version and
in Community. That is 37 of 41 -- the stable core is genuinely stable, which is the whole
premise of baking one vector per concept.
Edition is decided by the DECLARING MODULE'S manifest license (LGPL-3/AGPL-3 = community,
OEEL-1/OPL-1 = enterprise), not by absence from the community repository. See
tools/audit_odoo_edition.py for why that distinction matters.

community.method: class-body `_name = '<model>'` declaration in *.py, anchored; `_inherit` alone does not count
community.note_14_15_frozen: 14.0 and 15.0 last moved in 2024 and are out of Odoo's support window, so those two columns are settled permanently.

enterprise.source: official odoo_<ver>+e source packages (registered partner access)
enterprise.method: declaring module's __manifest__.py license: LGPL-3/AGPL-3 = community, OEEL-1/OPL-1 = enterprise
enterprise.gap: Enterprise 14.0, 15.0 and 16.0 were not available. account.asset's edition is directly verified for 17.0-19.0 and inferred for 14.0-16.0 from its absence across all six community branches.
enterprise.scale_note: Odoo 19.0 ships 716 OEEL-1 modules against 662 LGPL-3 -- more than half of Odoo is Enterprise. Irrelevant for the 41-model core, but it dominates any future corpus growth.

stock.route.note: Pure rename in addons/stock/models/stock_location.py; the CONCEPT exists in every supported version, only the identifier moved at 16.0. Deliberately carries NO `since`: `since` would mean the model did not exist below 16, which is false and would filter 14.0/15.0 instances out of an answer they can use under the old name. DECISIONS.md 12 guessed 17.0 for this rename -- it is 16.0.

product.tag.note: Does not exist in 14.0 or 15.0. Naming it for such an instance is the exact failure mode the version field exists to prevent.

account.asset.note: VERIFIED, not inferred (DECISIONS.md 17a): the declaring module odoo/addons/account_asset carries 'license': 'OEEL-1' and depends on the enterprise `accountant` module. Absent from community in all six branches. Applies to every version, so this is the edition axis rather than a range.
account.asset.provisional_reason: Edition verified directly for 17.0-19.0 only; Enterprise 14.0/15.0/16.0 source was not available. Below 17.0 this is inferred from absence across all six community branches. Run the corpus audit against those trees to clear it (corpus/README.md).

stock.valuation.layer.note: NOT a rename, and not in DECISIONS.md 12's list at all. Removed in 19.0: its fields (value, remaining_qty, remaining_value, account_move_id) moved onto stock.move itself. `product.value` in 19.0 is a different, narrower concept -- the history of MANUAL value updates -- so it is not the successor for a routing question. This is 12's 'a version genuinely reorganises semantics' case; routing an inventory-valuation question to stock.move on 19.0 is approximately right, but the card text still describes an 18.0-shaped world. Confirmed 2026-09-21 against Enterprise 19.0 as well: the removal is not an edition artifact, the model is gone in both editions.

_comment: How a running instance's edition is detected, verified by executing release.py from
both a community and an enterprise tree (DECISIONS.md 17a).
An earlier draft of this design assumed version_info[5] was the edition slot. It is NOT:
the field exists in the 6-tuple but is '' in BOTH editions. Odoo marks edition by
appending to `version` instead, via `version += '+e-<date>'` in the enterprise build.

version_axis.note: Clean major.minor. Prefer this over parsing server_version.

do_not_use.reason: '' in both community and enterprise builds; the slot exists in the tuple format but Odoo does not populate it.

edition_detection.open_saas: 19.0's release.py notes the MAJOR version can be an arbitrary string ('saas~xx') during release, so server_serie may be e.g. 'saas~16.3'. The mapping from a saas~ serie to a supported major is UNDECIDED -- an exact-match filter would return nothing for a whole class of Odoo Online instances.
